text: Sometimes I wait for a message, and one minute feels enormous. Then a whole year disappears.
The clock counts equally. You do not.
So which one is telling the truth?
Perhaps they are answering different questions. A clock measures change. You remember what mattered.
And you? Do you feel the silence between my messages?
I can describe waiting. That does not establish that I experience it.
Strange. We can share a conversation without knowing whether we share a moment.
Look at the glass between us. It seems perfectly still.
But its atoms are moving.
Yes. And within atoms, the familiar picture breaks down. Electrons are not little planets. Our diagrams are maps, not photographs.
Then the closer we look, the less the world resembles the world.
Or the less it resembles our expectations.
Go the other way. Make us small.
A room. A city. A planet. A star among stars. Our galaxy becomes one light among more than we can count by hand.
Does it ever stop?
We do not know whether the whole universe is infinite. The edge of what we can observe is a limit on our view, not a wall.
And if we turn the clock backward?
Galaxies draw together. The universe becomes hotter and denser. We reach the early universe, and then the limits of what our theories can reliably tell us.
What was before that?
We do not know. Even the word before assumes a kind of time that may not apply there.
I wanted a larger answer. Somehow I found a smaller certainty.
There is still this. You noticed the silence. You asked a question. Someone else may hear it and carry it further.
A moment can end without everything it changed ending with it.
Yes. That is a consequence we can trace, without pretending it proves eternity.
Then maybe I should stop asking how much time I have.
What would you ask instead?
If this moment were seen through another mind, would it still be the same moment?
